target.statement: EpiCoder's function-level synthetic data (380k samples) attains Halstead complexity of 10.66 unique operators, 44.32 unique operands, 56.98 total operators and 100.36 total operands, roughly doubling the strongest baseline (OSS-Instruct: 7.44 / 20.99 / 28.05 / 47.55; Code Alpaca: 4.83 / 8.22 / 10.66 / 15.89), i.e. the core claim that feature-tree synthesis yields far more complex code data.
target.dataset: EpiCoder function-level synthetic dataset (380k instructions) vs. Code Alpaca / CodeFeedback / Evol CodeAlpaca / OSS-Instruct

compute.basis: The target is a static metric over released synthetic code: download a few-GB dataset plus baseline datasets, then run an off-the-shelf Halstead/metrics Python parser (e.g. 'halstead'/radon) over each function with multiprocessing; no training, no LLM inference, CPU-only.

blockers: The headline results (Table 1 Pass@1, Figure 4 XFileDep) require supervised fine-tuning of 6.7B-7B models on 380k+53k samples - multiple GPU-days, not laptop-feasible
Table 2's exact sample set, deduplication and parser configuration are not specified, so reproduced averages will drift from the reported values

The paper states 'code and data are publicly available' but no direct URL for the 380k function-level dataset appears in the provided links; hosting (GitHub vs. HuggingFace) must be verified before download
Tables 3/4/15 (diversity, LLM-judge complexity) depend on GPT-4o API calls and cannot be reproduced without a paid closed model
title: EpiCoder: Encompassing Diversity and Complexity in Code Generation
